draft.title: The arrival of Christianity
card: Christianity came to Australia with the First Fleet in 1788. The fleet brought convicts, marines and officials from Britain, and a chaplain went with them.
The Church of England was the dominant church at first. It was the established church of Britain, and most colonists were English.
Other churches grew over time. These included the Catholic, Presbyterian and Methodist churches.
Christianity here came from outside. Aboriginal peoples already had their own spiritual traditions, which are covered in another point.
draft.remember: Christianity came in 1788 from Britain. The Church of England led at first, and other churches grew.

a.q: Which church was dominant in the colony when Christianity first arrived in 1788?
opts: The Church of England
The Catholic Church
The Presbyterian Church
The Methodist Church
a.why: The Church of England was the established church of Britain, and most early colonists were English. The Catholic, Presbyterian and Methodist churches grew over time but were not dominant at first.
a.clue: Think about which church was official in Britain.

b.q: Why was Christianity present in the colony from 1788?
opts: The First Fleet brought it from Britain
Aboriginal peoples brought it to the colony
Missionaries arrived in the colony in 1850
Gold miners introduced it in the colony
b.why: Christianity came with the First Fleet, which carried people from Britain. Gold miners and later missionaries are wrong because they came after 1788.
b.clue: Look at who and what sailed in 1788.

b.best: The First Fleet brought it from Britain

problems.detail: The question asks 'Why was Christianity present', but every option answers how or by whom it arrived. 'How did Christianity first reach the colony?' would match the options.

The distractor 'Missionaries arrived in the colony in 1850' suggests missionaries first came in 1850. Missionaries were active much earlier, from the 1790s, for example the London Missionary Society group in 1798. A distractor without a false date, or with a non-specific one, would avoid teaching a wrong date.

proposal.title: The arrival of Christianity
card: Christianity came to Australia with the First Fleet in 1788. The fleet carried convicts, marines and officials from Britain, and a Church of England chaplain sailed with them.
The Church of England was the dominant church at first. It was the official church of England, and the colony's governors and chaplains belonged to it.
Many convicts were Irish Catholics, but Catholic priests were not officially allowed to work in the colony until 1820. After that the Catholic Church grew quickly.
Other churches grew as more settlers arrived. Scottish settlers built up the Presbyterian Church, and the Methodist Church spread as well.
proposal.remember: The Church of England led from 1788, and the Catholic, Presbyterian and Methodist churches grew alongside it.

a.q: In the first years of the colony, which church held official standing?
opts: The Church of England

The Presbyterian Church
The Methodist Church
a.why: The Church of England was England's official church, and the governors and chaplains belonged to it. Many convicts were Catholic, but Catholic priests were not officially allowed until 1820, so that church was not dominant at first.
a.clue: Which church did the chaplain on the First Fleet belong to?

b.q: How did Christianity first reach the colony?
opts: It came with the First Fleet from Britain in 1788
Catholic priests brought it with the first convicts
Gold miners brought it during the 1850s gold rushes
Missionaries brought it before the colony was founded

b.clue: Think about who was on board the ships in 1788.

b.best: It came with the First Fleet from Britain in 1788

problems.detail: 'Catholic priests were not officially allowed to work in the colony until 1820' overstates the case. Governor King gave the convict priest Fr James Dixon conditional permission to say Mass in 1803, though this was withdrawn in 1804. What happened in 1820 was the arrival of the first officially appointed, government-paid Catholic chaplains, Therry and Conolly. Safer wording would be 'the first official Catholic chaplains did not arrive until 1820'. The same claim is repeated in both whys.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, and each has one clear right answer. One detail needs rewording: the 1820 claim about Catholic priests should be framed as the arrival of the first official Catholic chaplains, because a priest was briefly given permission in 1803.
